subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch and worker workloads, and what minimal public config/state surface should ship first?
rationale: The requested behavior spans public configuration, persisted/profile usage state, session stickiness, provider fallback, status output, and related issue boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Add a minimal opt-in pool contract
options.body: Preserve current defaults and add one canonical provider-profile pool routing surface with tests for cooldowns, session pinning, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Split into narrower existing issues
options.body: Keep #28847, #79604, and #91498 as separate workstreams and close or narrow this tracker once maintainers define how the pieces compose.

options.title: Defer native routing to plugins or sidecars
options.body: Keep core auth.order behavior unchanged and document sidecar/plugin approaches unless a missing core API blocks them.

recommendation.title: Add a minimal opt-in pool contract
recommendation.body: Preserve current defaults and add one canonical provider-profile pool routing surface with tests for cooldowns, session pinning, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses auth-profile config, provider identity, and fallback product policy where recent history repeatedly points to steipete.
